items.q: Q1. Can Indian students study civil engineering in Sweden after Class 12?
items.a: Yes. Indian students can apply if their secondary-school qualifications meet the university's general and programme-specific admission requirements, including the required mathematics and science subjects.

items.q: Q2. Are civil engineering bachelor's programmes in Sweden taught in English?
items.a: Many undergraduate engineering programmes are taught in Swedish. Students are advised to check the language of instruction of each program before applying. For example, Chalmers says its bachelor programs are taught in Swedish.

items.q: Q3. How long does it take to study civil engineering bachelor in Sweden?
items.a: The normal length of a bachelor’s level engineering program is three years or 180 ECTS credits. However, some engineering degrees are structured differently so students should check the exact length of their chosen course.

items.q: Q4. How much does it cost to study civil engineering in Sweden?
items.a: The amount you pay will depend on the university and the program. Students coming from countries outside the EU/EEA normally pay tuition fees, unless there is an exemption. And then there are living expenses. Applicants are advised to consult the full tuition schedule and make arrangements for accommodation, food, transport and other expenses.

items.q: Q5. After studying civil engineering in Sweden, what can I do?
items.a: Graduates may explore roles in construction, structural design, infrastructure, transportation, environmental engineering, and project coordination. Career opportunities depend on skills, experience, language proficiency, employer requirements, and eligibility to work in Sweden.
